messages.content: A physics experiment is being conducted where two objects are dropped from a height, neglecting air resistance. The first object is dropped with an initial speed of 0 m/s and the second object is dropped with an initial speed of 5 m/s. If the first object is in free fall for 10 seconds and the second object is in free fall for 7 seconds, can you calculate the final speed of both objects considering the acceleration due to gravity as -9.81 m/s^2?

function.name: calculate_final_speed
function.description: Calculate the final speed of an object in free fall after a certain time, neglecting air resistance. The acceleration due to gravity is considered as -9.81 m/s^2 Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_speed.description: The initial speed of the object in m/s. Default is 0 for an object at rest.

time.description: The time in seconds for which the object is in free fall.

gravity.description: The acceleration due to gravity. Default is -9.81 m/s^2. This is a float type value.

message.content:
**Formula**

For motion under constant gravitational acceleration \(g\) (with no air‑resistance),

\[
v_{\text{f}} \;=\; v_{0}\;+\;gt ,
\]

where  

* \(v_0\) – initial speed (positive when directed “upward” in our chosen coordinate system),  
* \(t\)   – elapsed time in seconds,  
* \(g\)   – gravitational acceleration (\(-9.81\,{\rm m/s^{2}}\)).

Because we take **upward as positive**, the acceleration due to gravity points *downward*, so it has the negative value \(-9.81~{\rm m/s^{2}}\).

---

### Object 1  
| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Initial speed \(v_0\) | \(0~{\rm m/s}\) |
| Time \(t\)            | \(10~{\rm s}\) |
| Acceleration \(g\)    | \(-9.81~{\rm m/s^{2}}\) |

\[
v_{\text{f},1}=0+(-9.81)(10)= -98.1~{\rm m/s}.
\]

The negative sign tells us the velocity vector points downward.  
Magnitude: **\(98.1~{\rm m/s}\)** downward.

---

### Object 2  
Assuming its initial drop speed is already directed downward:

| Quantity | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Initial speed \(v_0\) | \(-5~{\rm m/s}\) *(negative → downward)* |
| Time \(t\)            | \(7~{\rm s}\) |
| Acceleration \(g\)    | \(-9.81~{\rm m/s^{2}}\) |

\[
v_{\text{f},2}=(-5)+(-9.81)(7)
              = -5-68.67
              = -73.67~{\rm m/s}.
\]

Again, the negative sign denotes downward motion.  
Magnitude: **\(73.7~{\rm m/s}\)** downward.

---

#### Summary

| Object | Final speed (magnitude) | Direction |
|--------|-------------------------|-----------|
| 1      | \(98.1~{\rm m/s}\)       | Downward  |
| 2      | \(73.7~{\rm m/s}\)       | Downward  |

These calculations ignore air resistance and assume a uniform gravitational field of \(-9.81~{\rm m/s^{2}}\).
